title: OpenAI's first AI hardware aims for shipment by the end of 2026, with Chinese supply chain manufacturers deeply involved
excerpt: FIH Mobile, a Foxconn subsidiary, has secured orders for OpenAI's phone project and will participate in final assembly of related products. According to Securit
content_html:
FIH Mobile, a Foxconn subsidiary, has secured orders for OpenAI's phone project and will participate in final assembly of related products. According to Securities Times, Foxconn is also a major assembler of Apple's iPhone. If the OpenAI phone eventually reaches the market, it will formally enter the smartphone device market and may compete directly with existing smartphone brands over AI interaction experiences.

According to reports, OpenAI's first AI hardware product is scheduled to begin shipping by the end of 2026, with multiple Chinese manufacturers involved in the project. Among them, Luxshare Precision is exclusively responsible for final assembly and also supplies core components. However, OpenAI has not yet officially announced the product's specific form factor, order volume, or mass production schedule.

Earlier reports said the device is being developed in partnership between OpenAI and LoveFrom, the studio founded by former Apple Chief Design Officer Jony Ive. It may feature a screenless, donut-like design about the size of a hockey puck, integrate microphones, speakers, cameras, and multiple environmental sensors, rely mainly on voice interaction, and have environmental sensing capabilities. Rumored pricing is $300 to $400 (about 2,004 to 2,672 yuan), and the related information has not been officially confirmed.

From a supply chain perspective, OpenAI is pushing its AI capabilities to extend into standalone hardware devices. As Chinese manufacturers participate in final assembly and core component supply, competition in the AI hardware sector may further extend from models and software to end products.
